A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same offline reinforcement-learning domain-adaptation framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial formatting and theoretical revisions.

before.justification: V2 reports original CQL experiments on five Procgen games, evaluating dataset weights, source-domain discrepancies and target sample sizes in Figures 2–4 and Tables 1–4.

after.justification: V3 retains these original Procgen experiments in Figures 2–4 and Tables 1–4, with the tables relocated to Appendix C.1.

M1.justification: The weighted source/target TD-error objective in Equation (10) and its CQL implementation remain unchanged. Proposition 1 gives a generalized analytical solution under revised distribution assumptions; it does not introduce a different training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Caveflyer, Climber, Dodgeball, Maze and Miner using the same target levels [100,199] and source ranges [0,99], [25,124] and [50,149]. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The reported comparisons remain CQL with the same seven mixing weights, including target-only, source-only and equal-weight configurations. Neither version adds separately evaluated BCQ, IQL, H2O or ORIS baselines.

E3.justification: Table 5 retains the same sample-size grid, seven weights, 500 evaluation episodes, learning rate, batch size, network size and CQL settings. The figure captions likewise retain the experimental conditions; the changed hardware disclosure does not establish a revised evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The weight sensitivity, source-domain discrepancy and target-sample-size analyses are retained with the same evidence in Figures 2–4 and Tables 1–4. Moving the tables to the appendix does not add supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions retain identical plot error bars and the same mean/standard-deviation reporting across weights in Tables 1–2. No repeated-run counts, seed-reporting practices, confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: The plotted images in Figures 2–4 are identical, and every numerical row in Tables 1–4 matches after relocation. Reported returns, dispersions, optimal weights and empirical trends remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V3 replaces Assumption 2's exact equality of source, target-domain and empirical-target distributions with positive bounded ratios. Proposition 1 and Theorems 1–3 receive ratio-dependent expressions and revised proofs, while the variability and convergence-error definitions change. Corollaries 1–2 formalize endpoint and equal-ratio optimal weights; v2's explicit worst-case optimizer and its substituted bound are removed.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution bullets foreground the theoretical framework and explicitly qualify optimal-weight statements by simplifying assumptions, including closed-form availability. The central dataset trade-off, convergence-neighborhood and Procgen-support claims remain.

C2.justification: V3 explains that optimal weighting and the convergence neighborhood also depend on distribution-ratio bounds. However, it removes v2's explicit discussion that minimizing a performance bound need not optimize actual performance, including the associated endpoint caveats. The difficulty of estimating the dynamics gap and variance remains acknowledged.

D1.justification: The reported workstation changes from an RTX 3070 and i9-10900 at 2.80 GHz to an RTX A5000 with 24 GB and i9-10900X at 3.70 GHz in Appendix C.4. Implementation references, hyperparameters and the promise to release code upon publication remain unchanged; rerunning experiments is not established.

R1.justification: The cited-work set is unchanged. Related Work narrows the asserted research gap from prior theory about dynamics gaps and offline-RL performance generally to theory about dynamics gaps and dataset-weight selection, refining the novelty positioning.

P1.justification: V3 revises the title, abstract and contribution wording, changes 'Combining' to 'Balancing,' condenses the optimal-weight discussion and introduces numbered sections and appendix subsections. The overall narrative sequence and substantial portions of the surrounding prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The two-column main text becomes single-column with substantially different typography, spacing and figure sizing. Figure 1 moves into Related Work, and Tables 1–4 move from the main text to Appendix C.1. The underlying figure images and table contents are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 addresses a central restriction in v2 by deriving guarantees for unequal state-action distributions under bounded ratios, with corresponding proofs in Appendix A. It also aligns the main-text and appendix convergence-error definitions and qualifies the closed-form weight result. These substantially strengthen the theoretical contribution, despite continued full-coverage assumptions and the loss of an explicit caveat distinguishing bound optimization from actual performance optimization.
